term: first cause with universal priority-or-inclusion of its effect
definition: In Rutten's adjusted sense a first cause is an uncaused complete existence-producing cause with an effect M that is ontologically prior to OR includes every other caused effect. Ontological priority is his asymmetric existence-requirement notion, distinct from overlap or merely sharing a part. This is stronger than an uncaused object or an uncaused outgoing cause.
note: Primaryp124 states the prior-only definition; fn182p128 explicitly adds inclusion. The source asserts this full conclusion; no Lean proof of it is supplied here. Step5's passage from a caused shared part to M's priority remains a separate typed obligation. The generic body now fixes one M before ranging over ALL other caused effects, uses e ≤ M for inclusion and requirement M e ∧ ¬ requirement e M for priority. The arbitrary carrier and fixed PartialOrder are not restricted to modal actual objects. Existential requirement is explicitly primitive: y requires x to exist; its asymmetric part is defined transparently, not by a Boolean full-first-cause flag. Component/whole dependence is an illustrative candidate only; symmetric co-dependence, temporal precedence and sharing a part do not suffice. No independently certified real complete-production/requirement example is asserted. Requirement transitivity and its connection with production/parthood remain OPEN separate policies, not assumptions smuggled into this body. Existing sourced claim and locator are preserved; the binding is a working formal reconstruction, not new attribution verification.
